name: Singapore
description: A model of accessible urban design, Singapore offers seniors a seamless travel experience with its world-class MRT system featuring elevators at every station, English signage throughout, and excellent healthcare infrastructure.

topSpots.name: Gardens by the Bay
topSpots.notes: Fully wheelchair accessible with ramps and elevators, courtesy wheelchairs available, senior discount on entry

topSpots.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
topSpots.notes: Elevator access to observation deck, wide pathways, stunning city views without walking

topSpots.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
topSpots.notes: UNESCO World Heritage site, flat paved paths, benches every 50m, free entry, wheelchair rental

topSpots.name: National Museum of Singapore
topSpots.notes: Ramps at all entrances, elevators, accessible toilets, senior discount on admission

topSpots.name: Chinatown Heritage Centre
topSpots.notes: Restored shophouse with elevator access, local history exhibits, senior-friendly pacing

transport: MRT has elevators at every station, priority seating abundant. Senior MRT card offers discounted fares. Taxis readily available and affordable. Bus fleet 100% wheelchair accessible.
healthcare: World-class hospitals: Mount Elizabeth, Gleneagles, Singapore General Hospital. All English-speaking. Walk-in clinics at every neighborhood. Excellent pharmacy network.
highlights: Clean streets and abundant public restrooms
practicalTips: Get a Senior Citizen MRT card for discounted fares
Visit Gardens by the Bay early morning (9 AM) to avoid heat
Free shuttle bus around major tourist areas
Carry a water bottle
Most restaurants reduce spice on request

name: Taipei
description: Taipei offers the most generous senior benefits in Asia. Citizens aged 65+ ride the MRT for free, and foreign seniors can access many of the same discounts. The city is exceptionally safe with clean air, excellent healthcare, and food easy on digestion.

topSpots.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
topSpots.notes: Flat walking paths, wide steps with ramps, hourly changing of the guard

topSpots.name: Taipei 101
topSpots.notes: High-speed elevator to observatory, accessible restrooms, senior ticket price

topSpots.name: National Palace Museum
topSpots.notes: Wheelchair loan, ramps throughout, benches in every gallery, senior discount

topSpots.name: Beitou Hot Springs
topSpots.notes: Accessible public bathhouses, easy MRT access, gentle thermal pools

topSpots.name: Elephant Mountain
topSpots.notes: Easy paved trail at the base, suitable for gentle walks

transport: MRT with accessibility features at all stations. EasyCard for transit and stores. Seniors 65+ ride MRT for free with Foreign Visitor Senior EasyCard. Taxis very affordable.
healthcare: Excellent: National Taiwan University Hospital, Taipei Veterans General Hospital. English-speaking international clinics. Affordable dental care.
highlights: Free MRT for seniors 65+ (even foreign visitors)
Excellent street food with mild flavors
practicalTips: Get an EasyCard at any MRT station
Bring passport for senior MRT discounts
Visit night markets before 7 PM to avoid crowds
Many restaurants have English menus with pictures

name: Hong Kong
description: Hong Kong's legendary efficiency extends to its senior-friendly infrastructure. The MTR has elevators at most stations, the famous HK$2 travel scheme for seniors, and English is everywhere. Victoria Peak tram and world-class hospitals provide peace of mind.

topSpots.name: Victoria Peak (The Peak Tram)
topSpots.notes: Scenic tram ride with gentle incline, accessible Peak Tower with elevators and restaurants

topSpots.name: Star Ferry
topSpots.notes: Classic harbor crossing, flat boarding ramps, senior discount fare

topSpots.name: Hong Kong Park
topSpots.notes: Central park with paved paths, aviary, waterfall, accessible toilets

topSpots.name: Kowloon Walled City Park
topSpots.notes: Classical Chinese garden, flat paved paths, pavilions for resting

topSpots.name: Tian Tan Buddha (cable car)
topSpots.notes: Cable car with wheelchair option, accessible village at base

transport: MTR with elevators at most stations. Octopus Card for seamless tap-and-go. HK$2 travel scheme for seniors 65+. Taxis plentiful and affordable.
healthcare: World-class: Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital, Queen Mary Hospital. Excellent English-speaking doctors. International SOS clinic in Central.
highlights: HK$2 flat fare for seniors on MTR, buses, and ferries
practicalTips: Get the Senior Octopus Card for automated HK$2 fare
Check MTR accessibility maps
Visit the Peak before 3 PM to avoid crowds
Carry a light jacket
Use taxis for routes without MTR

name: Kyoto
description: Kyoto is the soul of traditional Japan. Major temples now have ramps, and Japan's omotenashi culture means staff go above and beyond to assist seniors. Zen gardens are naturally wheelchair-friendly. The city is clean, safe, and perfectly paced for older travelers.

topSpots.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
topSpots.notes: Wheelchair-accessible path around the pavilion, paved walkways, resting benches

topSpots.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
topSpots.notes: Flat paved path through the grove, accessible from station

topSpots.name: Philosopher Path
topSpots.notes: 2km flat walking path along canal, cherry blossoms, many benches

topSpots.name: Fushimi Inari (partial)
topSpots.notes: Lower section is wheelchair accessible, ground level is stunning

topSpots.name: Ryoan-ji Temple
topSpots.notes: Famous rock garden viewable from veranda, wheelchair loan available

transport: Look for low-floor non-step buses with ramps. Taxis are excellent and reasonably priced. JR Kyoto Station is a model of accessibility.
healthcare: Excellent: Kyoto University Hospital, Kyoto City Hospital. English-speaking clinics. 24-hour interpreter service available.
highlights: Zen gardens designed for contemplation at your own pace
Accessible toilets at all major attractions
practicalTips: Rent a taxi for half-day temple tour
Visit temples at opening time (8-9 AM)
Many restaurants have plastic food displays for easy ordering
Look for barrier-free signs

name: Tokyo
description: Tokyo is surprisingly accessible for seniors. The world's best transit system has priority seating, English audio announcements, and helpful staff. Parks like Ueno and Shinjuku Gyoen offer peaceful escapes. Incredible safety means exploring freely at any hour.

topSpots.name: Ueno Park
topSpots.notes: Flat paved paths, museums all wheelchair accessible, cherry blossoms

topSpots.name: Meiji Shrine
topSpots.notes: Wide paved forest path, wheelchair loan available, peaceful

topSpots.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
topSpots.notes: Fully accessible paths, many benches, tea house with ramp

topSpots.name: Asakusa Senso-ji
topSpots.notes: Main hall accessible by ramp, flat Nakamise street with benches

topSpots.name: teamLab Borderless
topSpots.notes: Fully wheelchair accessible, stunning digital art

transport: Extensive subway with elevators at most stations. JR Yamanote Line serves major areas. Priority seating culturally respected. Suica/Pasmo cards work everywhere.
healthcare: World-class: St. Luke's International Hospital, Tokyo Medical University Hospital. English-speaking clinics in central Tokyo.
highlights: Best public transit system in the world
practicalTips: Get a Suica or Pasmo card
Avoid rush hour (7:30-9:30 AM, 5-7 PM)
Priority seating is culturally respected
Look for barrier-free maps at stations

name: Chiang Mai
description: Chiang Mai is a favorite among international retirees. It's slow-paced, affordable, and offers excellent healthcare at Western prices. The Old City is compact and mostly flat with temples offering peaceful spaces. The expat community means English services are widely available.

topSpots.name: Doi Suthep (cable car)
topSpots.notes: Cable car to the top, temple has accessible areas, panoramic views

topSpots.name: Wat Phra Singh
topSpots.notes: Flat temple complex in Old City, gentle paths, shaded benches

topSpots.name: Night Bazaar
topSpots.notes: Flat walking area, early evening less crowded, seating available

topSpots.name: Nimman Area
topSpots.notes: Flat sidewalks, many cafes with outdoor seating

transport: Songthaews have high steps. Use Grab taxis instead. Private car with driver very affordable (~$30-40/day).
healthcare: Excellent: Chiangmai Ram Hospital, Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai (JCI accredited). Very affordable. Many doctors US/UK trained.
practicalTips: Use Grab instead of songthaews
Visit Old City in the morning when cooler
Bangkok Hospital has international patient desk

name: Seoul
description: Seoul combines cutting-edge technology with deep cultural traditions. The subway is modern with accessibility features, senior citizens ride at discounted rates, and Korea's hospitality culture extends to older visitors.

topSpots.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
topSpots.notes: Flat grounds, wheelchair loan, free entry for seniors 65+

topSpots.name: Namsan Cable Car
topSpots.notes: Scenic cable car to N Seoul Tower, fully accessible stations

topSpots.name: Seoul Forest
topSpots.notes: Large park with flat paved paths, deer enclosure, butterfly garden

topSpots.name: Hangang River Cruise
topSpots.notes: Flat boarding, indoor seating, gentle cruise, senior discount

transport: Seoul Subway with elevators at most stations. Seniors 65+ ride subway for free. T-money card works everywhere. Taxis affordable.
healthcare: Excellent: Severance Hospital, Samsung Medical Center. Many English-speaking doctors. Leading medical tourism destination.
practicalTips: Get a T-money card at any convenience store
Show passport for senior subway discounts
Use Seoul Subway app with elevator locations

name: Penang
description: Penang is a sensory feast that's surprisingly accessible for seniors. George Town's UNESCO heritage zone is largely flat and walkable with countless cafes for rest breaks. The food is legendary and affordable, English is widely spoken.

topSpots.name: Pinang Peranakan Mansion
topSpots.notes: Ground floor access, air-conditioned, senior ticket price

topSpots.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
topSpots.notes: Escalators up the hill, accessible prayer areas

topSpots.name: Penang Hill (funicular)
topSpots.notes: Funicular to the top, accessible viewing decks

topSpots.name: Clan Jetties
topSpots.notes: Flat wooden boardwalks over water, benches for resting

transport: Grab recommended for seniors (~$2-5/ride). CAT free shuttle bus in George Town.
healthcare: Good: Penang Adventist Hospital, Island Hospital, Gleneagles Penang. English-speaking doctors.
highlights: UNESCO George Town flat and walkable
practicalTips: Use Grab within George Town
Visit street art early morning (before 9 AM)
Penang Hill is 5°C cooler

name: Hoi An
description: Hoi An is a beautifully preserved ancient trading port. The Old Town is largely flat and car-free, making it comfortable for walking at a gentle pace. Lantern-lit streets, affordable tailors, and exquisite cuisine make this a favorite among mature travelers.

topSpots.name: Old Town Lantern Streets
topSpots.notes: Flat mostly pedestrianized area, benches along the river

topSpots.name: Japanese Covered Bridge
topSpots.notes: Short iconic bridge, flat approach, beautiful photo spot

topSpots.name: An Bang Beach
topSpots.notes: Flat path to beach, restaurants with seating, gentle waves

topSpots.name: Cooking Classes
topSpots.notes: Ground floor, seated experience, gentle-paced

transport: Very walkable Old Town. Private car hire cheap (~$15-20/day). Da Nang Airport 45 min away.
healthcare: Limited: Hoi An General Hospital. For serious needs, Da Nang (45 min). Travel insurance strongly recommended.
highlights: Cooking classes for all mobility levels
practicalTips: Wear comfortable shoes with good grip
Visit Old Town late afternoon (4 PM)
Set menu lunches are great value ($5-8)

name: Bali (Ubud)
description: Ubud is Bali's cultural heart, known for wellness retreats and spiritual atmosphere. While the terrain is hilly, the area excels in spa treatments, gentle yoga, and healthy food. Private drivers make it accessible door-to-door.

topSpots.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
topSpots.notes: Paved paths through sanctuary, shaded, flat walking

topSpots.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
topSpots.notes: Viewing deck without hiking down, coffee tasting nearby

topSpots.name: Ubud Palace
topSpots.notes: Central, flat grounds, free entry, evening dance performances

topSpots.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
topSpots.notes: 2km paved ridge path, mostly flat, benches

transport: Private driver best option (~$30-40/day). Grab works in Ubud. Airport transfer 1.5-2 hours.
healthcare: Adequate: Ubud Clinic (international standard). Travel insurance with evacuation strongly recommended.
practicalTips: Hire a private driver for your stay
Request ground floor rooms
Bring insect repellent

name: Bangkok
description: Bangkok's superpower is world-class healthcare at Western prices. Hospitals like Bumrungrad and Bangkok Hospital are JCI-accredited. While heat and traffic are intense, affordable taxis and Grab cars make the city manageable.

topSpots.name: Grand Palace
topSpots.notes: Large complex, mostly flat, shaded areas, accessible toilets

topSpots.name: Wat Pho (Reclining Buddha)
topSpots.notes: Flat temple complex, ramps at entrance, massage on-site

topSpots.name: Asiatique Riverfront
topSpots.notes: Flat walkways, seating throughout, restaurants with river views

transport: BTS Skytrain elevators at most stations. MRT better for accessibility. Taxis very affordable. Grab recommended.
healthcare: World-class: Bumrungrad International, Bangkok Hospital (JCI), Samitivej. English-speaking doctors, US/UK trained.
practicalTips: Use BTS or Grab instead of walking long distances
Visit temples early (8-9 AM)
Carry a hand fan and water

name: Kuala Lumpur
description: Kuala Lumpur offers a comfortable introduction to Southeast Asia for seniors. English is widely spoken, infrastructure modern, and very affordable. Free city buses and massive shopping malls provide air-conditioned comfort with great accessibility.

topSpots.name: Petronas Towers & KLCC Park
topSpots.notes: Elevator to skybridge, park with flat paved paths, benches

topSpots.name: Batu Caves (cable car)
topSpots.notes: Cable car avoids 272 steps, amazing Hindu temple cave

topSpots.name: Islamic Arts Museum
topSpots.notes: Accessible galleries, restaurant with great views

topSpots.name: KL Bird Park
topSpots.notes: World's largest free-flight aviary, flat paved paths

transport: Go KL City Bus FREE covers tourist areas. MRT/LRT modern with elevators. Grab affordable.
healthcare: Excellent: Prince Court Medical Centre, Pantai Hospital, Gleneagles KL. English-speaking doctors.
highlights: Modern accessible transit with free city buses
practicalTips: Use free Go KL buses for sightseeing
Stay in KLCC/Bukit Bintang area
Ask for senior discounts!

name: Da Nang
description: Da Nang is Vietnam's most livable city. A beach destination with modern airport, wide boulevards, and beautiful coastline. Less chaotic than Hanoi or Saigon, ideal for seniors wanting beach relaxation with cultural options nearby.

topSpots.name: My Khe Beach
topSpots.notes: Long flat promenade, gentle waves, accessible beach access

topSpots.name: Marble Mountains (elevator)
topSpots.notes: Elevator to the top, cave temples, panoramic views

topSpots.name: Linh Ung Pagoda
topSpots.notes: Flat temple grounds, giant Buddha statue, ocean views

transport: Walkable along beach road. Taxis cheap and metered. Airport small, 15 min from beach.
healthcare: Good: Da Nang Family Hospital, Vinmec Da Nang. Adequate for non-emergency care.
highlights: Less chaotic than Hanoi or Saigon
practicalTips: Stay in My Khe Beach area
Visit Marble Mountains early (7:30 AM)
Wide pavements for walking

name: Luang Prabang
description: Luang Prabang is a UNESCO World Heritage town where time stands still. Nestled between the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers, this former royal capital is compact, walkable, and deeply peaceful. Limited medical facilities but unmatched tranquility.

topSpots.name: Royal Palace Museum
topSpots.notes: Flat grounds, beautiful colonial building, accessible

topSpots.name: Night Market
topSpots.notes: Flat walking area, handicrafts and textiles

topSpots.name: Mekong River Cruise
topSpots.notes: Gentle boat ride, seated, sunset cruise option

topSpots.name: Kuang Si Waterfalls (lower)
topSpots.notes: Lower pools accessible by flat path

transport: Very walkable town center. Tuk-tuks for longer trips. Airport 15 min from town.
healthcare: Limited: Luang Prabang Provincial Hospital. International Clinic for minor issues. Evacuation insurance essential.
practicalTips: Watch alms-giving from respectful distance (~5:30-6 AM)
Take a Mekong sunset cruise
Bring cash

name: Siem Reap
description: Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor Wat. While temples have steep steps, main temples offer accessible ground-level exploration. Tuk-tuks make getting around easy. The town has a buzzing food scene and the Cambodian people are famously warm.

topSpots.name: Angkor Wat (ground level)
topSpots.notes: Flat paths around the moat, stunning photos without climbing

topSpots.name: Ta Prohm (Tomb Raider)
topSpots.notes: Paved central path through tree-root ruins

topSpots.name: Angkor National Museum
topSpots.notes: Air-conditioned, wheelchair accessible, excellent exhibits

transport: Covered tuk-tuks. Private car with driver ~$30-40/day recommended for seniors.
healthcare: Limited: Royal Angkor International Hospital. For serious needs, Bangkok (1 hr flight). Evacuation insurance essential.
practicalTips: Hire a private car instead of tuk-tuk
Visit Angkor Wat at sunrise
Buy multi-day pass for relaxed pace
